questions.q: What does a data governance maturity model actually measure, per the lesson?
options: How many regulations an organization is subject to
How capable an organization is at governing its data in defined, repeatable, measured practice — not good intentions
The dollar amount spent on data tools
The total number of employees in the data department
questions.explain: A maturity model scores actual, repeatable practice against ordered levels — not stated intentions or aspirations.

questions.q: Which organization developed the Data Management Maturity (DMM) model that applies a five-level process-maturity structure to data specifically?
questions.explain: CMMI's Data Management Maturity model applies CMMI's familiar five-level structure (Initial through Optimizing) to data management, across six key themes.

questions.q: According to the lesson, where do most organizations actually land on these maturity models?
options: Exactly evenly spread across all levels
In the lower-middle levels — aware and reactive, without proactive organization-wide discipline
At the very top level, fully optimized
Below the lowest defined level entirely
questions.explain: The lesson reports this as the honest, widely documented finding across these models — most organizations cluster in the lower-middle levels, not the top.

questions.q: What does the lesson call a maturity score that has no attached action plan or roadmap?
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that a score reported upward as a badge, with no specific gaps identified or roadmap attached, is 'governance theater, not governance work.'

questions.q: How many governance disciplines does IBM's Data Governance Maturity Model assess, per the lesson?
options: One single overall score with no disciplines
questions.explain: IBM's model assesses eleven governance disciplines (such as data risk management and data quality management) across four stages: Aware, Controlled, Managed, and Optimized.
